raw_response:
1. The figure does not show a benchmark line at 50 datasets, and English in 2018–2019 appears below 50 (around the 30–40 range). So this plot alone doesn’t support the claim that English crossed 50 or that there was a “significant” increase specifically due to crossing that threshold.

2. Bengali in 2019 is not 10 in the figure (it’s about 2), while Spanish in 2019 is about 4. So Spanish has roughly twice as many datasets as Bengali in 2019.

3. The figure only provides data through 2022 and does not include a projection method, so a 2025 projection isn’t directly supported. From 2017–2021 Arabic rises from ~3 to ~7 (about +1 per year on average), while “All other” rises from ~15 to ~40 (about +6–7 per year), so “All other” grows faster over that period.
